title: GenWave Jingle Pack Manifest
description: The <slug>.jingle-pack.json shape a GenWave station fetches for a kind:"jingle-pack" catalog entry (app repo SPEC F165, PLAN T410/T412). A jingle pack ships background music beds, stings, and station IDs (SPEC F165.3's `role` enum) — real audio bytes, unlike a persona/theme/show/ad-pack's pure-data manifests. `additionalProperties` is false at every level, closed like ad-pack: STORY-400 AC6 needs a top-level `attribution` array (as opposed to the per-asset `attribution` object below) to be an unknown-property rejection, since attribution belongs to the ASSET that needs it, never to the pack as a whole. `packName` becomes the station's `library.media.artist` for every spot played from this pack (SPEC F165.2). `license` is closed to `CC0`/`CC-BY` (SPEC F165.4) — CC-BY-SA and everything else is refused by the enum itself, not a validate.py rule, because there is nothing conditional about it: no third value is ever legal here.
$comment: Every `(?![\s\S])` suffix below is the portable absolute-end-of-string anchor the rest of this catalog's schemas use in place of a bare `$`/`\Z` (Python re's own `$` matches before a trailing newline; `\Z` is not ECMA-262/.NET-portable).

packName.description: Shelf title / attribution name for the pack. Becomes the station's `library.media.artist` for every spot played from this pack (SPEC F165.2).

assets.description: One entry per audio asset this pack carries.

file.description: The asset filename, sibling to the manifest. One of three audio containers (wav/mp3/flac) — tools/validate.py's `jingle-pack-audio-magic` separately checks the bytes actually match the extension's own magic, not just the name.

role.description: What this asset is for (SPEC F165.3): `bed` = background music under a generated spot, `sting` = a short standalone musical accent, `station_id` = a spoken/musical station identification clip.

license.description: Closed to CC0 and CC-BY (SPEC F165.4) — CC-BY-SA's share-alike obligation, and every other licence, is refused by this enum itself.

creator.description: Who to credit, exactly as the licence requires.

sourceUrl.description: Where the original asset came from. `format: uri` is deliberately NOT set here — no FormatChecker is wired into any validator this repo's own tools/validate.py constructs (validate_schema builds `validator_cls(schema)` with none), so `format: uri` would be silently inert, not a gate. This pattern is the actual gate: scheme-anchored (`^https?://`), forbids whitespace/angle-brackets/quotes in the remainder (T411 review round 1 finding 3 — a value like `https:// not a uri at all \n<script>` matched the old prefix-only pattern), and end-anchored with `(?![\s\S])` per this file's own top-level $comment.

license.description: Repeats the item's own `license` — always `CC-BY` here, since a CC0 asset must carry no `attribution` at all (see the per-item conditional below).

else.description: A CC0 asset has nothing to attribute (STORY-400 AC1) — carrying an `attribution` object anyway is a contributor mistake worth failing CI on, not a harmless extra.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the asset's bytes. tools/validate.py's `jingle-pack-sha256-mismatch` recomputes this from the file actually on disk and rejects a mismatch — this schema only pins the SHAPE.
